content.text: No redline is warranted here — the minimum sits within a one-year term with an unconditional Client exit and no shortfall penalty. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes the only purchase commitment on us: a monthly floor for Hosting and Support Services (amounts still blank). That commitment sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred usage-only position, and is acceptable on its material terms: (i) the Agreement runs "for a period of 1 year" and renews only in successive one-year periods, with either party free to give notice of intent not to renew 30 days before year end (p0078), so the floor never extends beyond the current 12-month term; (ii) Section 14 gives us an unconditional election to terminate — TrueLink continues services only "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate" (p0079) — so we can exit the minimum on roughly a month's notice; and (iii) the minimum operates purely as a fee floor: we pay up to the minimum for the months we take service, with no shortfall charge, accelerated balance, liquidated damages or other penalty anywhere in the document. Minor points noted but not flagged: the exit tail can run up to about 60 days rather than a clean 30 days, the exit is expressed as termination rather than partial reduction, and the dollar figures plus the internal cross-references ("minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" in Section 6, and "Subject to Section 4" in Section 14, where the minimums actually appear in Section 5) should be completed and conformed at signature. Separately, the requirement in Section 3(i) to order credit reports through the Interface is a sourcing condition that applies only when we choose to use the Interface — Section 2(a) expressly leaves us "free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other" system — so it is not a volume commitment under this rule.
